description: Hi, I'm Tasneem, a builder from Qatar who loves turning big ideas into simple apps that real people can use. I build web apps with AI, React and computer vision, and I just shipped a live AI makeup coach. I'm drawn to Field Shift because farmers here face less water and hotter summers every year. I'd love teammates who enjoy Python and NASA data, design, or storytelling. Let's build something that matters and have fun doing it!
summary: Farm Twin is a web app that helps farmers plan a full year on their own field. A farmer pins the field on a satellite map. The app works out whether it's a greenhouse, an open field or a pivot. It then gives a month-by-month plan for what to plant and when, with heat, frost, salt and water warnings. In Qatar it corrects NASA POWER weather for the coast, which cut the daily-high error from 2.18 °C to 1.75 °C. It also maps surface salt from satellite images in Qatar (F1 0.94 on 157 checked spots). In the US it works from raw NASA POWER weather, shown on two California demo farms: an almond and pistachio orchard in the San Joaquin Valley and a canal-irrigated field in the Imperial Valley. There the plan adds California's Cal/OSHA heat rule for farm workers and flags very thirsty crops when the farmer wants to save water. Everywhere else outside Qatar it also uses raw NASA weather and a 28-crop table with each crop's frost and heat limits. Plans look ahead to the 2035 climate where NASA projections exist, which is not the case in California.
details: Farm Twin is a web app that helps a farmer plan a full year on their own field. The farmer pins the field on a satellite map and confirms "Is this your field?". The app then gives a 12-month plan: what to plant and when, greenhouse cooling difficulty, water need per crop, surface salt seen from space, and ranked next-crop rotations, with heat, frost, salt and water warnings. Every answer has "Agree / No, because…", and the farmer's answers change the next result. It works in English and Arabic (right-to-left).
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources): daily weather, AG community
NASA POWER API documentation (parameters T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, T2MDEW, RH2M, WS2M, WD2M, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, PRECTOTCORR)
NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis (the weather model behind NASA POWER)
projectRefs: ESA Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A imagery (via Copernicus Data Space)
Microsoft Planetary Computer (access to Landsat, Sentinel-2, NASADEM, WorldCover)
NOAA Global Surface Summary of the Day (weather stations used to train the coast correction)
Esri World Imagery (satellite base map and farm photos)
Natural Earth (coastline, for distance to the sea)
FAO-29 water quality for agriculture (salt limits)
FAO greenhouse temperature limits (FAO publication used in our crop table)
Cal/OSHA heat illness prevention rule, Title 8 §3395 (California heat note)
Claude Code (Anthropic), used to write code and text
Helsinki-NLP opus-mt-en-ar (used to compare the Arabic text)
